Dialog_CancelTip

data.name: Tray_ShowTip
data.value: Opens the window with your controllers and their calibration.

data.name: Tray_LearningTip

data.name: Tray_QuitTip
data.value: Quits DS4 Handler completely. The virtual controllers go away too.

data.name: Tray_HintText
data.value: Your controllers keep working. Click the icon in the notification area to open the window again, or choose Quit there.

data.name: Main_EmptyText
data.value: Connect a DualShock 4 or DualSense. It shows up as a tab at the top by itself.

data.name: Main_EmptyUsb
data.value: Plug in the cable. That's all you need to do.

data.name: Main_EmptyBluetooth
data.value: Hold PS and Share (or Create) until the light blinks fast. Then pair it in Windows under Settings › Bluetooth.

data.name: Main_HidHideOffTip
data.value: Hide from games is off (see Settings). Some games then see two controllers.

data.name: Main_HidHideActiveTip
data.value: HidHide hides your real controllers from games, so they only see the Xbox controller.

data.name: Main_HidHideMissingTip
data.value: HidHide is not installed. Without HidHide, some games see your controller twice.

data.name: Main_HidHideBusyTip
data.value: Another program (HidHide Configuration Client or DS4Windows) has HidHide open. Close it and click Check again.

data.name: Main_HidHideErrorTip

data.name: Notice_ViGEmMissingText
data.value: Without ViGEmBus, DS4 Handler can't create an Xbox controller, so games get no input. You can still see all values here. Install ViGEmBus (free), then restart the app.

data.name: Notice_ViGEmFailedText
data.value: ViGEmBus could not be opened ({0}). Restart your PC; if that doesn't help, reinstall ViGEmBus.

data.name: Notice_HidHideMissingText
data.value: Without HidHide, some games see both your PlayStation controller and the Xbox controller, so buttons respond twice. Install HidHide (free), then click Check again. No double input? Then turn HidHide off in Settings.

data.name: Notice_HidHideBusyText
data.value: Another program has HidHide open, usually the HidHide configuration tool or DS4Windows. Close that program and click Check again.

data.name: Notice_HidHideErrorText
data.value: HidHide gave an unexpected error. Restart your PC or reinstall HidHide.

data.name: Notice_BlockedOne
data.value: A controller is in use by another program

data.name: Notice_BlockedMany
data.value: {0} controllers are in use by another program

data.name: Notice_BlockedText
data.value: DS4 Handler sees a controller but can't open it. Close DS4Windows or other controller software. The app tries again every few seconds.

data.name: Settings_HidHideReady
data.value: HidHide is installed and ready to use.

data.name: Settings_HidHideMissing
data.value: HidHide is not installed. Download it for free with the button below, then click Check again.

data.name: Settings_HidHideBusy
data.value: HidHide is busy: close the HidHide configuration tool (or DS4Windows) and click Check again.

data.name: Settings_HidHideError
data.value: HidHide gave an unexpected error. See the log file.

data.name: Settings_StartWithWindowsText
data.value: The app starts when you sign in, so your controller works right away.

data.name: Settings_StartMinimizedText
data.value: Only as an icon in the notification area next to the clock.

data.name: Settings_AutoUpdateText
data.value: Your profiles and settings are kept when you update.

data.name: Settings_UseHidHideText
data.value: Games only see the virtual controller. Turn this on per controller with 'Hide from games'.

data.name: Settings_UnhideOnExitText
data.value: After quitting, games see your PlayStation controller as usual again.

data.name: Settings_AboutText
data.value: Your PlayStation controller works in games as an Xbox 360 or DualShock 4 controller. The app learns your stick drift and trigger wear by itself and corrects them.

data.name: Settings_LanguageText
data.value: For all text in the app.

data.name: Settings_LanguageTip
data.value: Choose the language of the app. The new language is used after the app restarts.

data.name: Settings_LanguageRestartNote
data.value: The new language is used after a restart.

data.name: Settings_RestartNowTip
data.value: Closes DS4 Handler and starts it again right away, in the new language. Your profiles and settings are kept.

data.name: Controller_PressedButtonsGame
data.value: Pressed buttons as the game sees them

data.name: Controller_CalibrationIntro
data.value: The app learns by itself while you play: where the center of your sticks is and how far your triggers really press. You don't need to do anything here, unless you want it to go faster.

data.name: Controller_KeepLearningText
data.value: Drift and wear change slowly. The app keeps up with that.

data.name: Controller_JitterFilterText
data.value: Removes the small wobble when you let go of the stick.

data.name: Controller_StartOverText
data.value: Throws away everything the app has learned about this controller.

data.name: Profiles_Intro
data.value: Each controller gets its own profile, recognized by its MAC address. Bring along a friend's profile with Import.

data.name: Profiles_None
data.value: No profiles yet. Connect a controller or import a profile.

data.name: Remap_PressToFind
data.value: Press a button to find it.

data.name: Remap_List
data.value: Buttons and what the game gets

data.name: Tuning_SavedNow
data.value: Changes are saved right away to this controller's profile.

data.name: Tuning_SendToGameNote
data.value: Every reading is fastest and fine for almost everyone.

data.name: Tip_Brand
data.value: DS4 Handler makes your PlayStation controller work in games as an Xbox or DualShock 4 controller, and fixes stick drift and worn triggers by itself.

data.name: Tip_NavSettings
data.value: Start with Windows, HidHide (hide your real controller from games), updates, info about the app, and quit.

data.name: Tip_ControllerTab
data.value: Click to view this controller. The dot shows how it's doing: green works, orange is waiting or still learning, red is a problem.

data.name: Tip_NoControllerTab
data.value: As soon as you connect a controller, it shows up here as a tab. Click to see how to connect a controller.

data.name: Tip_DriversSection
data.value: The two free tools DS4 Handler uses. ViGEmBus creates the controller games see; HidHide hides your real controller so games don't see it twice. Click to open Settings.

data.name: Tip_ControllerTitle
data.value: The name of this controller's profile. You can change it under Profiles.

data.name: Tip_TabLive
data.value: See live what your sticks and triggers do, and what the game gets.

data.name: Tip_TabCalibration
data.value: What the app has learned about drift and wear, centering the sticks and measuring the triggers.

data.name: Tip_TabAdjust
data.value: Set how this controller responds: deadzones, curves, triggers and speed. Changes are saved to the controller's profile right away.

data.name: Tip_TabButtons
data.value: Choose per button what the game gets: another button, a key on your keyboard, or nothing. You can also swap the sticks. Changes are saved to the controller's profile right away.

data.name: Tip_CalibrationSummary
data.value: A short summary of what the app has learned about this controller. Click to open Calibration and see everything.

data.name: Tip_ControllerName
data.value: The type of PlayStation controller. In games, the app makes it work as an Xbox 360 or DualShock 4 controller (see 'Games see it as').

data.name: Tip_ControllerId
data.value: This controller's unique address. Its calibration is saved under it, so it uses the same profile over USB and Bluetooth.

data.name: Tip_ControllerIdUnstable
data.value: This controller's address could not be read, so its calibration is tied to this USB port: on another port it starts learning from scratch.

data.name: Tip_Usb
data.value: Connected with a USB cable. That gives the fastest response and charges the controller at the same time.

data.name: Tip_Bluetooth
data.value: Connected wirelessly over Bluetooth. Noticing lag? Use a cable or move the controller closer to your PC.

data.name: Tip_ReportRate
data.value: How many times per second the controller sends its state. Higher is smoother; 250 or more is fine.

data.name: Tip_Latency
data.value: How long the app takes from a controller reading until the virtual controller for games is updated. Under 0.1 ms is excellent; over 1 ms points to a busy PC. The longest gap shows whether the connection stutters: over USB it should be around 4 ms, over Bluetooth around your chosen polling rate. Much higher means interference or a weak Bluetooth signal.

data.name: Tip_StickView
data.value: Live view of the stick. • Gray dot: where the stick really is. • Blue dot: what the game gets after correction. • Orange dashed ring: the deadzone around the learned rest point.

data.name: Tip_Deadzone
data.value: Stick movement inside this circle is ignored, so drift doesn't move your character. The size is learned automatically: as small as possible, as large as needed.

data.name: Tip_TriggerBar
data.value: Thin gray line: how far you really press the trigger. Thick blue bar: what the game gets. Orange marks: the learned rest point and end point (your 100%).

data.name: Tip_LegendRaw
data.value: Gray: the controller's real position, without correction.

data.name: Tip_LegendOutput
data.value: Blue: what the game gets, after correcting for drift and wear.

data.name: Tip_LegendDeadzone
data.value: Orange: the rest point and end point the app has learned for this trigger.

data.name: Tip_Pad
data.value: Which buttons are pressed right now. Choose whether you see your real controller or the virtual controller the game gets.

data.name: Tip_PadInput
data.value: What you're pressing on your controller right now, without correction.

data.name: Tip_PadOutput
data.value: What the game gets from the virtual controller right now. Xbox 360 has no touchpad click or Mute button, so those never reach the game.

data.name: Tip_CalibrationSection
data.value: This shows in plain words what the app has learned about this controller. It happens by itself while you play and is saved per controller.

data.name: Tip_Learning
data.value: On: the app keeps learning how this controller behaves while you play (drift, worn triggers). Off: what was already learned keeps working, but nothing changes anymore.

data.name: Tip_JitterFilter
data.value: On: stick jitter is filtered out. The app measures how much a stick shakes when you hold it still (released or at a fixed position) and filters exactly as much as needed. A good stick won't notice a thing. Fast movements pass through without noticeable delay; only holding still and aiming very slowly get calmer. Off: the stick goes to the game unfiltered, as before.

data.name: Tip_HideFromGames
data.value: Hides your real PlayStation controller from games, so they only see this app's Xbox controller. That prevents double input. Works through HidHide. A game that's already running needs a restart (or reconnect the controller).

data.name: Tip_HideUnavailable
data.value: Hiding works through the free program HidHide. Turn HidHide on in Settings, or install it first.

data.name: Tip_Output
data.value: What kind of controller games see this controller as.

data.name: Tip_OutputXbox
data.value: Xbox 360: works in almost every PC game. Pick this if you're not sure. Games then show Xbox buttons (A, B, X, Y).

data.name: Tip_OutputDs4
data.value: DualShock 4: for games that support PlayStation controllers themselves (for example through Steam's PlayStation support); they then show PlayStation buttons. Note: the motion sensor and touchpad are not passed on (yet). Turn on 'Hide from games' so games only see the virtual DualShock 4 and not your real controller too.

data.name: Tip_Reset
data.value: Forget everything learned for this controller and start over with factory values. Handy after a repair or when the correction is no longer right.

data.name: Tip_Recenter
data.value: Use this if your stick suddenly has much more drift than before. Then let go of both sticks; the new rest point is measured right away. Normal drift is learned automatically, you don't need to do anything for that.

data.name: Tip_CancelGuided
data.value: Stops the assistant. What was already learned stays.

data.name: Tip_CalibrateTrigger
data.value: The fastest way to fix a trigger that no longer reaches 100%: press it all the way a few times and that point becomes your new 100%. Automatic learning works too, but needs more presses.

data.name: Tip_StickSummary
data.value: What was learned for this stick: where it rests (drift), how big the deadzone is, and whether it reaches the edge in every direction.

data.name: Tip_TriggerSummary
data.value: What was learned for this trigger: how far it still goes and whether that is scaled up to 100%.

data.name: Tip_EmptyState
data.value: As soon as you connect a DualShock 4 or DualSense, it shows up here by itself. Bluetooth? Pair the controller in Windows settings first (hold PS + Share until the light blinks).

data.name: Tip_StartWithWindows
data.value: Start DS4 Handler automatically when you sign in, so your controller works in games right away.

data.name: Tip_StartMinimized
data.value: Start without a window, only with an icon in the system tray (bottom right, by the clock). Double-click that icon to open the window.

data.name: Tip_HidHideEnabled
data.value: Use HidHide to hide your real controllers from games. Without hiding, some games see two controllers and buttons respond twice. DS4 Handler adds itself to the exceptions list, so the app itself can still see the controller. Note: this also turns on HidHide's general hide switch. That also applies to devices you hid in HidHide yourself before.

data.name: Tip_UnhideOnExit
data.value: On: when you quit DS4 Handler, games and other programs (like Steam or an emulator) see your controller normally again. Off: the controller stays hidden after quitting too. Handy if the app always runs, but without the app it won't work in games.

data.name: Tip_RecheckHidHide
data.value: Check again whether HidHide is available, for example after you installed it or closed the HidHide configuration.

data.name: Tip_DownloadHidHide
data.value: Opens the HidHide download page (free, from the same maker as ViGEmBus).

data.name: Tip_DownloadViGEm
data.value: Opens the download page of ViGEmBus, the driver that creates the virtual Xbox controller. Restart the app after installing.

data.name: Tip_OpenProfiles
data.value: Opens the folder with each controller's learned calibration.

data.name: Tip_CheckForUpdates
data.value: At startup (and then twice a day), checks GitHub for a new version of DS4 Handler. You'll see what's new at the top and can update with one click. Nothing is ever installed without you clicking.

data.name: Tip_CheckNow
data.value: Check right now whether there's a new version.

data.name: Tip_UpdateNow
data.value: Downloads the new version and installs it over the old one. The app closes briefly and then restarts by itself. Your profiles, calibration and settings are kept.

data.name: Tip_UpdateLater
data.value: Hide this message until the next time the app starts.

data.name: Tip_UpdateDownloadPage
data.value: Opens the download page of the new version on GitHub.

data.name: Tip_OpenLog
data.value: Opens the log file. Handy to send along when something doesn't work.

data.name: Tip_Quit
data.value: Quits DS4 Handler completely. The virtual Xbox controllers then disappear.

data.name: Tip_DriverReady
data.value: ViGEmBus is installed: games see your controller as an Xbox 360 controller.

data.name: Tip_DriverMissing
data.value: ViGEmBus is missing. Without this driver the app can't create an Xbox controller and games get no input.

data.name: Tip_DriverChecking
data.value: Checking whether the Xbox driver (ViGEmBus) is present.

data.name: Tip_NavProfiles
data.value: All controllers this PC knows, with their learned calibration. Name them, share or copy a profile, or bring in a friend's profile.

data.name: Tip_ProfilesIntro
data.value: Every controller gets its own profile, recognized by its MAC address. So it uses the same profile over USB and Bluetooth.

data.name: Tip_ProfileName
data.value: A name you choose, for example 'Sam's controller'. Leave it empty to show the controller type. The name doesn't change the calibration.

data.name: Tip_ProfileRename
data.value: Give this profile a different name. Press Enter or click elsewhere to save.

data.name: Tip_ProfileMac
data.value: The MAC address: this controller's unique address. The app recognizes it by this, over USB and over Bluetooth.

data.name: Tip_ProfileNoMac
data.value: No MAC address could be read from this controller. So the profile is tied to the USB port it was on.

data.name: Tip_ProfileModel
data.value: The controller type of this profile.

data.name: Tip_ProfileLastSeen
data.value: When this controller was last connected to this PC.

data.name: Tip_ProfileSummary
data.value: A short summary of what was learned for this controller: how far the triggers go and whether the sticks have drift.

data.name: Tip_ProfileUsedBy
data.value: Other connected controllers that share this profile: they learn together in the same calibration.

data.name: Tip_ProfileCopy
data.value: Copy what was learned for this controller to another controller. Whatever was learned there is overwritten.

data.name: Tip_ProfileCopyNone
data.value: Copying is only possible once something has been learned for this profile and there's another profile.

data.name: Tip_ProfileExport
data.value: Save this profile as a file, for example to give to a friend or as a backup.

data.name: Tip_ProfileImport
data.value: Load a profile file, for example a friend's. It's tied to their controller (MAC address): connect it and it works right away with its own calibration.

data.name: Tip_ProfileDelete
data.value: Delete this profile and its name. If you connect the controller again later, it starts learning from scratch.

data.name: Tip_ProfileDeleteBlocked
data.value: A profile used by a connected controller can't be deleted. Disconnect the controller first or pick another profile for it.

data.name: Tip_ProfileChoose
data.value: Choose which profile this controller learns into. By default its own profile; you can also let it share the profile of another controller of the same type. Two connected controllers can't use the same profile at the same time.

data.name: Tip_LinkOwn
data.value: The controller learns into its own profile (recommended).

data.name: Tip_LinkShared
data.value: The controller uses and improves the calibration of this other profile.

data.name: Tip_ProfileOnCard
data.value: The profile this controller learns into. You can change it under Profiles.

data.name: Tip_ProfileOwnOnCard
data.value: This profile belongs to this controller. What the app learns and what you tune is saved here. You can pick another profile under Profiles.

data.name: Tip_ProfileBlockedOnCard
data.value: This controller's profile is already used by another connected controller. To keep both from overwriting the same file, this controller runs on factory values for now and nothing is saved. Pick another profile under Profiles or reconnect it later.

data.name: Tip_OpenProfileFolder
data.value: Opens the folder with the profile files.

data.name: Tip_TunePicker
data.value: Choose what you want to tune. You see one part at a time.

data.name: Tip_TuneSticks
data.value: Deadzones, shape, curve and sensitivity of both sticks.

data.name: Tip_TuneTriggers
data.value: Deadzone, end point and curve of L2 and R2.

data.name: Tip_TuneSpeed
data.value: How often the controller measures and how often the game gets an update.

data.name: Tip_TuneSaved
data.value: No need to save. Every change goes into this controller's profile right away.

data.name: Tip_CurveStick
data.value: How the stick responds: to the right is how far you push, up is what the game gets. The gray part is the extra deadzone, the dotted line is 1 to 1. Updates as you move the sliders.

data.name: Tip_CurveTrigger
data.value: How the trigger responds: to the right is how far you press, up is what the game gets. The gray part is the extra deadzone, the dotted line is 1 to 1. Updates as you move the sliders.

data.name: Tip_TuneSection
data.value: These settings come on top of what the app has learned by itself. They're saved in the controller's profile.

data.name: Tip_TuneResetAll
data.value: Set all Tuning settings for this controller back to default. What the app has learned stays.

data.name: Tip_TuneResetSection
data.value: Set only this part back to default.

data.name: Tip_TuneShape
data.value: The shape of the extra deadzone around the center of the stick.

data.name: Tip_TuneShapeRadial
data.value: Round: the stick first has to leave a circle around the center before anything happens. Feels the same in every direction. This is the normal choice.

data.name: Tip_TuneShapeSquare
data.value: Square: the stick only counts once you push far enough on at least one axis; small diagonal movements around the center are ignored. Many Rocket League players use this for calm, straight steering.

data.name: Tip_TuneShapeAxial
data.value: Cross: each direction (left-right and up-down) has its own deadzone, so a small sideways wobble doesn't leak into a straight push. Anti-deadzone and sensitivity then also work per axis. Diagonals do feel a bit more angular.

data.name: Tip_TuneInner
data.value: Extra deadzone: the stick has to move this far before the game notices anything. Comes on top of the deadzone the app has learned by itself. Handy if your character or camera still moves slightly while you do nothing. With Square and Cross it can be less large, and the higher the end point, the lower the maximum, so you always keep a working range.

data.name: Tip_TuneOuter
data.value: End point: the stick gives full output before it hits the edge. Handy if the edge of the stick is hard to reach, for example because of a thick stick cap or a worn stick.

data.name: Tip_TuneAnti
data.value: Anti-deadzone: as soon as the stick leaves the deadzone, the output jumps straight to at least this percentage. Use this if the game has its own deadzone: then your stick responds right away, instead of you having to push a bit first. Start small, around 10%. With Cross this applies per axis.

data.name: Tip_TuneTriggerAnti
data.value: Anti-deadzone: as soon as you press the trigger past its deadzone, the output jumps straight to at least this percentage. Handy if the game itself only responds after pressing a bit. Start small, around 10%.

data.name: Tip_TuneCurve
data.value: Curve: how the stick or trigger responds between start and end. 1.00 is straight: 1 to 1. Above 1 is calmer at the start (precise aiming) and stronger at the end. Below 1 is quick on small movements instead.

data.name: Tip_TuneSensitivity
data.value: Sensitivity: multiplies the stick's movement. Above 1× you reach full output before the stick hits the edge; below 1× you never quite reach full. The result never goes above 100%. With Cross this works per axis.

data.name: Tip_TuneFilterResponse
data.value: Response: the app filters out jitter from a worn stick without making the stick lag while you aim. Calm (left) removes the most jitter. Fast (right) follows stops and changes of direction a little more tightly, but more jitter gets through. Only has an effect if the app has measured jitter on this stick; a new stick won't notice anything.

data.name: Tip_TuneSquareOutput
data.value: Square output: pushing diagonally gives 100% on both axes, instead of about 70% per axis at most. Handy for games where you want full speed diagonally. Don't turn this on if a game already uses a square range itself.

data.name: Tip_TuneInvertX
data.value: Swaps left and right for this stick.

data.name: Tip_TuneInvertY
data.value: Swaps up and down for this stick. Handy for flying or an 'inverted' camera.

data.name: Tip_TuneTriggerInner
data.value: Extra deadzone: the trigger has to be pressed this far before the game notices anything. Handy if a trigger still responds slightly while you release it.

data.name: Tip_TuneTriggerOuter
data.value: End point: the trigger gives full output before it's pressed all the way. Handy for faster accelerating or shooting.

data.name: Tip_TunePoll
data.value: How many times per second the controller sends its state. Higher gives less lag but uses more battery. 250 or more is fine for most games. Only available for a DualShock 4 over Bluetooth. Over USB the controller sets the speed itself.

data.name: Tip_TunePollUnavailable
data.value: This is only possible for a DualShock 4 over Bluetooth. Over USB, and with a DualSense, the controller decides itself how often it measures.

data.name: Tip_TuneOutputRate
data.value: How many times per second the virtual controller is updated for games. 'Every reading' is the fastest and fine for almost everyone. Limiting it is only needed on a slow PC or a game that chokes on lots of updates.

data.name: Tip_RemapPicture
data.value: Your controller, live. Press a button: that button's row lights up in the list, so you find it right away.

data.name: Tip_RemapTarget
data.value: What the game gets when you press this button. Pick another button, 'Keyboard…' for a key (for example for a voice or chat key), or 'Off' to ignore the button. Two buttons may have the same target.

data.name: Tip_RemapTriggerTarget
data.value: A button on a trigger gives that trigger fully pressed. A trigger on the other trigger stays analog (L2 and R2 swap). A trigger on a button counts from half pressed.

data.name: Tip_RemapResetRow
data.value: This button does what's printed on it again.

data.name: Tip_RemapResetAll
data.value: Set all buttons and the sticks for this controller back to default. Tuning and calibration stay as they are.

data.name: Tip_RemapSwapSticks
data.value: Swaps the left and right stick: what you do with the left, the game gets as the right, and vice versa. Your Tuning settings stay with your real stick. L3 and R3 don't swap along; you choose those per button below.

data.name: Tip_RemapCapture
data.value: Press the key the game should get when you press this button. Esc stops without changing anything.

data.name: Tip_RemapChanged
data.value: This button does something other than what's printed on it.

data.name: Calib_StickGuided
data.value: {0}: let go of the stick… measuring the rest point.

data.name: Calib_StickLearning
data.value: {0}: still learning — let go of the stick now and then.

data.name: Calib_StickRestsAt
data.value: {0} rests at ({1}, {2}) instead of the center — that point now counts as the center.

data.name: Calib_StickWeakReach
data.value: Only reaches {0} of the edge in some directions — scaled up to 100%.

data.name: Calib_StickJitterOff
data.value: Jitter on the {0}: {1} (jitter filter is off).

data.name: Calib_TriggerGuided
data.value: {0}: assistant running — press the trigger all the way a few times.

data.name: Calib_TriggerLearning
data.value: {0}: still learning — press it all the way a few times while playing. Until then, the full range is used.

data.name: Calib_TriggerFullRange
data.value: {0} reaches the full range — no correction needed. {1}

data.name: Calib_TriggerScaled
data.value: {0} goes up to {1} — scaled up to 100%. {2}

data.name: Calib_ResetMessage
data.value: Everything the app has learned about this {0} (drift, deadzone, trigger end points) will be forgotten. The controller starts over with factory values and then learns again.

data.name: Latency_Now
data.value: Now: {0} ms on average, slowest {1} ms. Longest gap from the controller: {2} ms.

data.name: Battery_Low
data.value: Battery: {0}%. Almost empty: plug in the cable to charge.

data.name: Battery_Wireless
data.value: Battery: {0}%. Lasts about 4 to 8 hours on a full charge.

data.name: Battery_Usb
data.value: Battery: {0}%. The controller charges over the USB cable.

data.name: Status_WaitingInputTip
data.value: The controller is connected but isn't sending input (yet). On Bluetooth: press the PS button. If this stays, reconnect it.

data.name: Status_Ds4ActiveTip
data.value: Games now see this controller as a (virtual) DualShock 4, with rumble. The calibration corrections are already applied. Turn on 'Hide from games' so games don't also see your real controller.

data.name: Status_XboxActiveTip
data.value: Games now see this controller as an Xbox 360 controller, with rumble. The calibration corrections are already applied.

data.name: Status_MeasureOnlyTip
data.value: ViGEmBus is missing, so there's no virtual controller for games. You still see all values here and the app keeps learning. Install ViGEmBus (see the message at the top).

data.name: Status_VirtualFailedTip
data.value: The virtual controller couldn't be created: {0}. Reconnect the controller or restart your PC.

data.name: Profile_CardBlocked
data.value: Profile in use — running without saving

data.name: Hide_HiddenTip
data.value: Games only see the Xbox controller, not your real PlayStation controller. A game that was already running: restart it or reconnect the controller.

data.name: Hide_FailedTip
data.value: Hiding didn't work, so games may see this controller twice. {0}

data.name: Hide_FailedSeeNotice
data.value: Check the message at the top or Settings › HidHide.

data.name: Profile_NeverConnected
data.value: Not connected to this PC yet

data.name: Profile_LinkBlocked
data.value: Profile in use by another controller: running without saving

data.name: Profile_CopyMessage

data.name: Profile_ExportDone
data.value: Profile saved. Send the file to your friend; in DS4 Handler they choose Profiles › Import.

data.name: Profile_DeleteMessage
data.value: Everything learned for '{0}' ({1}) is deleted, along with the name. If you connect this controller again later, it starts learning from scratch.

data.name: Profile_ImportTooLarge

data.name: Profile_ImportDone

data.value: Every button on this {0} does what's printed on it again, keys are unlinked and the sticks go back to their own place. Tuning and calibration stay as they are.

data.name: HidHide_SettingsReadOnly
data.value: Settings couldn't be read or saved safely, so the app isn't hiding any controllers right now (otherwise they could stay hidden). Restart the app; the log file has more details.

data.name: HidHide_SharedHost
data.value: The app is running through dotnet.exe. Start DS4Handler.exe itself, otherwise HidHide can't add the app as an exception and the controller stays visible.

data.name: HidHide_PathFailed
data.value: The folder DS4 Handler is in couldn't be passed to HidHide (for example a network drive). Put the app on a local drive.

data.name: HidHide_Busy
data.value: HidHide is busy: another program (like HidHide Configuration Client or DS4Windows) has it open. Close that program and click Check again.

data.name: Library_SameProfile
data.value: Source and target are the same profile.

data.value: Nothing has been learned for this profile yet to copy.
